qualifier: This page is for you if you are a lawyer who moved to a new city after marriage and left a practice, a court and a network behind.
symptom_title: New city, no court, no contacts
symptom: You had built something in your old city: a court you knew, clerks who knew you, clients who called. Marriage brought you here, and that practice stayed behind.

Here, nobody knows your name. The local bar has its own seniors and its own circles. Sometimes even the court language is different. Starting again feels like being a first-year junior with years of experience.
You still read every agreement your family signs, and you still spot the gaps. What you do not have is a place to use that skill here.
outcome_title: A career that does not depend on your court address
outcome: Tech law is the work lawyers do for technology businesses on contracts, privacy, compliance and disputes. A startup client needs the document, not your court address. The work can be done from any city with a laptop and a connection.
Starting a tech law career could let you build a practice that moves with you. Clients could come from India, the US, the UK, Canada or Europe. If you move again, the career comes along.
alternatives_title: Ways lawyers who relocate usually try to restart

alternatives.t: Joining a senior in the new city's courts
alternatives.why: You start as a junior again, in a bar where seniority is local. Years of experience elsewhere count for little in a new chamber.

alternatives.t: Applying to firms in your new city
alternatives.why: Many firm openings travel through local networks you have not built yet. Your old city's references do not carry far.

alternatives.t: Travelling back to handle old matters
alternatives.why: It keeps a few clients for a while. The trips are tiring and costly, and the practice still thins out.

reframe_title: You did not lose your skill. You lost your location.
reframe: What you lost in the move is a network tied to one court. Your skill came with you. The question is where to point it, and that is a positioning choice, not a test of effort.

Court years train you to read a document for what is missing, then write the notice or reply that fixes it. Reviewing a startup's terms is the same reading. One of the Day 1 message templates starts by telling a founder you reviewed their terms and noticed 3 missing clauses.
cost_title: What waiting to settle in costs
cost: Settling into a new city takes time, and that is normal. But each month without legal work makes the next step feel larger. Three evenings from your new home, for Rs 10, is a small first move.
role_h2: What tech law work looks like for a lawyer who moved city after marriage
role: Finding clients starts online. On Day 1 the camp shows how lawyers reach startups in the US, UK, Canada, Europe and India, with demos on Y Combinator and Shark Tank. The target is small startups before Series A, with fewer than 20 people.

The first piece of work is often a review. You read a founder's terms, list what is missing, and offer to fix it. That is the reading you did on notices and pleadings, now done for a business. It is also a task you can finish in one evening.

Networking replaces your old bar circle. Day 2 and Day 3 show how to connect with US, UK and Canadian lawyers through their directories, by helping first. Your new network can be built from your new home.
first_artifact: On Day 1 you draft a software development agreement with the faculty, clause by clause, and learn the two outreach message templates. That gives you a document you understand and a way to start conversations, both from wherever you now live.
longer_term: The 6-month plan asks for 2 hours a day: 1 for learning and 1 for outreach. Outreach starts in week 1, with LinkedIn posts and an hour a day pitching startups. In a city where you know nobody, that hour builds the network your old court used to give you. By month 6 you could have a set of contacts and drafts that belong to no single city.

faq.q: I do not know anyone in this city. Can I still find work?
faq.a: The camp's outreach is online, to startups and lawyers in several countries. It does not depend on local contacts.

faq.q: Do I have to give up the idea of practising in court here?
faq.a: No. Tech law can run beside a new court practice or replace it. You can decide that later, once you have seen the work.

faq.q: As an enrolled advocate, can I approach startups at all?
faq.a: The rules restrict advertising and soliciting. The approach the camp teaches is to find a genuine issue in a public document and share a useful observation, not to ask for a brief. For anything specific, ask your State Bar Council.

faq.q: My old practice was litigation. Is that enough to start?
faq.a: Litigation trains close reading and drafting, which are the base of contract review. The camp adds the tech side on Day 1, from SLAs and APIs to SaaS.

closing_title: Lawyers who moved city after marriage: start a tech law career wherever you live now
closing: If you moved city after marriage and left a practice behind, tech law lets you build again without a local court or network. In three live evenings you draft a software contract and learn how lawyers reach startups abroad. All three evenings cost Rs 10 incl. GST, refundable.
